ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$ with side length 2, point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. Connect $BE$ and fold $\triangle ABE$ along $BE$ to obtain $\triangle FBE$. $BF$ intersects $AC$ at point $G$. What is the length of $CG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $BF$ to meet $CD$ at $H$, and connect $EH$,\\
since $\triangle FBE$ is obtained by folding $\triangle ABE$ along $BE$,\\
therefore $EA=EF$, $\angle EFB=\angle EAB=90^\circ$,\\
since $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, and the side length of square $ABCD$ is $2$,\\
therefore $EA=ED=1$,\\
therefore $ED=EF=1$,\\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
therefore $\angle D=\angle EFB=\angle EFH=90^\circ$,\\
in $Rt\triangle EDH$ and $Rt\triangle EFH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}ED=EF\\ EH=EH\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $Rt\triangle EDH \cong Rt\triangle EFH\ (HL)$,\\
therefore $\angle DEH=\angle FEH$,\\
also since $\angle AEB=\angle FEB$,\\
therefore $\angle DEH+\angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABE+\angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ABE=\angle DEH$,\\
therefore $\triangle DHE \sim \triangle AEB$,\\
therefore $\frac{DH}{DE}=\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $DH=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $CH=CD−DH=2−\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
since $CH\parallel AB$,\\
therefore $\triangle HGC \sim \triangle BGA$,\\
therefore $\frac{CG}{AG}=\frac{CH}{AB}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
therefore $CG=\frac{3}{4}AG=\frac{3}{4}(AC−CG)$,\\
since $AB=2$, $CB=2$, $\angle CBA=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $AC=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
therefore $CG=\frac{3}{4}(2\sqrt{2}−CG)$,\\
therefore $CG=\boxed{\frac{6}{7}\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; E is on the left side AD, and the shown position is near the midpoint of AD; BE is connected, and the diagonal AC is drawn; the folded point F is in the upper part inside the square, and the line segment BF intersects the diagonal AC at G. Then reason: Extend BF according to the figure so that it intersects CD at H, and connect EH. Because triangle ABE is folded along BE to obtain triangle FBE, the symmetric point of A with respect to BE is F, therefore EA=EF, ∠EFB=∠EAB=90°, and ∠AEB=∠FEB. It is known that the side length of the square is 2, and E is the midpoint of AD, so AE=ED=1, hence ED=EF=1. Since ABCD is a square, CD is perpendicular to AD, so ∠EDH=90°; also because H is on the extension of BF, and ∠EFB=90°, ∠EFH=90°. In right triangles EDH and EFH, ED=EF, and EH is the common hypotenuse, so Rt△EDH≅Rt△EFH (HL). Therefore ∠DEH=∠FEH. Also from the folding, ∠AEB=∠FEB. Because ED and EA are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠DEH and ∠FEH are equal, and combined with ∠AEB=∠FEB, it can be obtained that ∠DEH+∠AEB=90°. But in right triangle AEB, ∠ABE+∠AEB=90°, so ∠ABE=∠DEH. Thus △DHE and △AEB are similar. The corresponding side ratio is DH/DE=AE/AB=1/2. Because DE=1, DH=1/2. Also CD=2, so CH=CD-DH=2-1/2=3/2. Because CH is parallel to AB, and G is the intersection point of BH and AC, △HGC∼△BGA. From the similarity ratio, CG/AG=CH/AB=(3/2)/2=3/4. Let CG=x, then AG=AC-CG. The side length of the square is 2, so AC=2√2. Therefore x=(3/4)(2√2-x). Solving gives 4x=6√2-3x, that is, 7x=6√2, so CG=6√2/7.

method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一个正方形ABCD，A在左下，B在右下，C在右上，D在左上；E在左边AD上，图示位置为AD的中点附近；连接了BE，画出了对角线AC；折叠后的点F在正方形内部偏上方，线段BF与对角线AC相交于G。

再推理：按图形延长BF，使它与CD交于H，并连接EH。因为三角形ABE沿BE折叠得到三角形FBE，所以A关于BE的对称点是F，因此EA=EF，∠EFB=∠EAB=90°，且∠AEB=∠FEB。已知正方形边长为2，E是AD的中点，所以AE=ED=1，从而ED=EF=1。

由于ABCD是正方形，CD垂直AD，所以∠EDH=90°；又因为H在BF的延长线上，且∠EFB=90°，所以∠EFH=90°。在直角三角形EDH和EFH中，ED=EF，EH为公共斜边，所以Rt△EDH≅Rt△EFH（HL）。因此∠DEH=∠FEH。

又由折叠可得∠AEB=∠FEB。因为ED与EA在同一直线上且方向相反，∠DEH与∠FEH相等，结合∠AEB=∠FEB，可得∠DEH+∠AEB=90°。而在直角三角形AEB中，∠ABE+∠AEB=90°，所以∠ABE=∠DEH。

于是△DHE与△AEB相似。对应边比为DH/DE=AE/AB=1/2。因为DE=1，所以DH=1/2。又CD=2，所以CH=CD-DH=2-1/2=3/2。

因为CH平行AB，且G是BH与AC的交点，所以△HGC∼△BGA。由相似比得CG/AG=CH/AB=(3/2)/2=3/4。设CG=x，则AG=AC-CG。正方形边长为2，所以AC=2√2。因此x=(3/4)(2√2-x)。解得4x=6√2-3x，即7x=6√2，所以CG=6√2/7。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$ with side length 2, point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. Connect $BE$ and fold $\triangle ABE$ along $BE$ to obtain $\triangle FBE$. $BF$ intersects $AC$ at point $G$. What is the length of $CG$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $BF$ to meet $CD$ at $H$, and connect $EH$,\\
since $\triangle FBE$ is obtained by folding $\triangle ABE$ along $BE$,\\
therefore $EA=EF$, $\angle EFB=\angle EAB=90^\circ$,\\
since $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, and the side length of square $ABCD$ is 2,\\
therefore $EA=ED=1$,\\
therefore $ED=EF=1$,\\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
therefore $\angle D=\angle EFB=\angle EFH=90^\circ$,\\
in $Rt\triangle EDH$ and $Rt\triangle EFH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}ED=EF\\ EH=EH\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $Rt\triangle EDH \cong Rt\triangle EFH\ (HL)$,\\
therefore $\angle DEH=\angle FEH$,\\
also since $\angle AEB=\angle FEB$,\\
therefore $\angle DEH+\angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABE+\angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ABE=\angle DEH$,\\
therefore $\triangle DHE \sim \triangle AEB$,\\
therefore $\frac{DH}{DE}=\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $DH=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
therefore $CH=CD−DH=2−\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
since $CH\parallel AB$,\\
therefore $\triangle HGC \sim \triangle BGA$,\\
therefore $\frac{CG}{AG}=\frac{CH}{AB}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
therefore $CG=\frac{3}{4}AG=\frac{3}{4}(AC−CG)$,\\
since $AB=2$, $CB=2$, $\angle CBA=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $AC=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
therefore $CG=\frac{3}{4}(2\sqrt{2}−CG)$,\\
therefore $CG=\boxed{\frac{6}{7}\sqrt{2}}$

First describe the image: In the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; E is on the left side AD, and the shown position is near the midpoint of AD; BE is connected, and the diagonal AC is drawn; the folded point F is in the upper part inside the square, and the line segment BF intersects the diagonal AC at G.

Then reason: Extend BF according to the figure so that it intersects CD at H, and connect EH. Because triangle ABE is folded along BE to obtain triangle FBE, the symmetric point of A with respect to BE is F, therefore EA=EF, ∠EFB=∠EAB=90°, and ∠AEB=∠FEB. It is known that the side length of the square is 2, and E is the midpoint of AD, so AE=ED=1, hence ED=EF=1.

Since ABCD is a square, CD is perpendicular to AD, so ∠EDH=90°; also because H is on the extension of BF, and ∠EFB=90°, ∠EFH=90°. In right triangles EDH and EFH, ED=EF, and EH is the common hypotenuse, so Rt△EDH≅Rt△EFH (HL). Therefore ∠DEH=∠FEH.

Also from the folding, ∠AEB=∠FEB. Because ED and EA are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠DEH and ∠FEH are equal, and combined with ∠AEB=∠FEB, it can be obtained that ∠DEH+∠AEB=90°. But in right triangle AEB, ∠ABE+∠AEB=90°, so ∠ABE=∠DEH.

Thus △DHE and △AEB are similar. The corresponding side ratio is DH/DE=AE/AB=1/2. Because DE=1, DH=1/2. Also CD=2, so CH=CD-DH=2-1/2=3/2.

Because CH is parallel to AB, and G is the intersection point of BH and AC, △HGC∼△BGA. From the similarity ratio, CG/AG=CH/AB=(3/2)/2=3/4. Let CG=x, then AG=AC-CG. The side length of the square is 2, so AC=2√2. Therefore x=(3/4)(2√2-x). Solving gives 4x=6√2-3x, that is, 7x=6√2, so CG=6√2/7.

First describe the image: In the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; E is on the left side AD, and the shown position is near the midpoint of AD; BE is connected, and the diagonal AC is drawn; the folded point F is in the upper part inside the square, and the line segment BF intersects the diagonal AC at G.

Then reason: Extend BF according to the figure so that it intersects CD at H, and connect EH. Because triangle ABE is folded along BE to obtain triangle FBE, the symmetric point of A with respect to BE is F, therefore EA=EF, ∠EFB=∠EAB=90°, and ∠AEB=∠FEB. It is known that the side length of the square is 2, and E is the midpoint of AD, so AE=ED=1, hence ED=EF=1.

Since ABCD is a square, CD is perpendicular to AD, so ∠EDH=90°; also because H is on the extension of BF, and ∠EFB=90°, ∠EFH=90°. In right triangles EDH and EFH, ED=EF, and EH is the common hypotenuse, so Rt△EDH≅Rt△EFH (HL). Therefore ∠DEH=∠FEH.

Also from the folding, ∠AEB=∠FEB. Because ED and EA are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠DEH and ∠FEH are equal, and combined with ∠AEB=∠FEB, it can be obtained that ∠DEH+∠AEB=90°. But in right triangle AEB, ∠ABE+∠AEB=90°, so ∠ABE=∠DEH.

Thus △DHE and △AEB are similar. The corresponding side ratio is DH/DE=AE/AB=1/2. Because DE=1, DH=1/2. Also CD=2, so CH=CD-DH=2-1/2=3/2.

Because CH is parallel to AB, and G is the intersection point of BH and AC, △HGC∼△BGA. From the similarity ratio, CG/AG=CH/AB=(3/2)/2=3/4. Let CG=x, then AG=AC-CG. The side length of the square is 2, so AC=2√2. Therefore x=(3/4)(2√2-x). Solving gives 4x=6√2-3x, that is, 7x=6√2, so CG=6√2/7.
